title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

"""Core SVEAD implementation (paper Sections 4.1-4.4, Algorithm 1).

Pipeline per partition k = 1..t
-------------------------------
1. sample m anchors uniformly from the row indices *without replacement*
   (R1, Section 4.1 "Anchor Sampling");
2. assign every point to its nearest anchor by Euclidean distance -- an
   *implicit* Voronoi diagram, no cell boundaries or vertices are built
   (R2 / R11, Section 4.1 "Voronoi Cell Assignment", Eq. (1));
3. for every non-empty cell compute delta_max and delta_mean *before* any
   scoring (R4, Algorithm 1 lines 7-10);
4. score each point as s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean (R3, Eq. (3));
   a cell that contains only its anchor (|C| == 1) is skipped for that
   partition (Section 4.2);
5. average the per-partition scores (R6, Eq. (5)).

The implementation is chunked and O(n*m*d*t) (R12).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, Tuple

import numpy as np

# Keep the (chunk x m) squared-distance block under ~32 MB of float64.
_MAX_BLOCK_ELEMENTS = 4_000_000


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R1: anchor sampling
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample ``m`` distinct row indices uniformly without replacement."""
    m = int(min(m, n))
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R2 / R11: implicit Voronoi assignment
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _chunk_size(m: int) -> int:
    return max(1, int(_MAX_BLOCK_ELEMENTS // max(1, m)))


def assign_cells(
    X: np.ndarray, anchor_idx: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int | None = None
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Assign every row of ``X`` to its nearest anchor.

    Returns ``(cell_ids, delta)`` where ``cell_ids[i]`` is the index (into
    ``anchor_idx``) of the nearest anchor of row ``i`` and ``delta[i]`` is the
    exact Euclidean distance to that anchor.  Ties are broken towards the
    lowest anchor index (``np.argmin`` returns the first minimum).
    """
    X = np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    A = np.ascontiguousarray(X[anchor_idx], dtype=np.float64)
    n, d = X.shape
    m = A.shape[0]
    if chunk_rows is None:
        chunk_rows = _chunk_size(m)

    a_sq = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", A, A)
    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)

    for start in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        stop = min(start + chunk_rows, n)
        block = X[start:stop]
        # ||x - a||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||a||^2 - 2 x.a  (used only for the argmin)
        d2 = (
            np.einsum("ij,ij->i", block, block)[:, None]
            + a_sq[None, :]
            - 2.0 * (block @ A.T)
        )
        j = np.argmin(d2, axis=1)
        cell[start:stop] = j
        # exact distance to the winning anchor (avoids expansion round-off)
        diff = block - A[j]
        delta[start:stop] = np.sqrt(np.einsum("ij,ij->i", diff, diff))
    return cell, delta


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R4: per-cell statistics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def cell_stats(cell: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, m: int) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Per-cell ``delta_max`` / ``delta_mean`` / size, computed before scoring."""
    n = cell.shape[0]
    order = np.argsort(cell, kind="stable")
    sorted_cell = cell[order]
    uniq, starts = np.unique(sorted_cell, return_index=True)
    sizes = np.diff(np.append(starts, n)).astype(np.int64)

    d_sorted = delta[order]
    d_max = np.maximum.reduceat(d_sorted, starts)
    d_sum = np.add.reduceat(d_sorted, starts)
    d_mean = d_sum / sizes

    dmax_arr = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    dmean_arr = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    size_arr = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.int64)
    dmax_arr[uniq] = d_max
    dmean_arr[uniq] = d_mean
    size_arr[uniq] = sizes
    return {
        "delta_max": dmax_arr,
        "delta_mean": dmean_arr,
        "size": size_arr,
        "n_nonempty": int(uniq.size),

"""Full cardio protocol: m-grid x 5 repeats at t=100 (paper Sections 5.1, R7/R8/R9/R10).

Writes ``results/per_m_table.csv`` and ``results/raw_cardio.json``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead.data import load_cardio  # noqa: E402
from svead.metrics import evaluate, summarize  # noqa: E402
from svead.svead_core import svead_score  # noqa: E402

M_GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]  # {2^1, ..., 2^8}
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
T = 100


def run(m_grid=None, seeds=None, t=T, out_dir="results"):
    m_grid = list(m_grid or M_GRID)
    seeds = list(seeds or SEEDS)
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    X, y, prov = load_cardio()
    records = []
    t_start = time.perf_counter()
    for m in m_grid:
        for seed in seeds:
            scores, scores_over_t, diag = svead_score(
                X, m, t=t, seed=seed, return_diagnostics=True
            )
            ev = evaluate(scores, y)
            ev_t = evaluate(scores_over_t, y)
            rec = {
                "m": int(m),
                "seed": int(seed),
                "t": int(t),
                **ev,
                "auc_roc_divide_by_t": ev_t["auc_roc"],
                "auc_pr_divide_by_t": ev_t["auc_pr"],
                **diag,
            }
            records.append(rec)
            print(
                f"m={m:4d} seed={seed} auc_roc={ev['auc_roc']:.4f} "
                f"auc_pr={ev['auc_pr']:.4f} skip={diag['skipped_fraction_mean']:.4f} "
                f"({diag['partition_seconds_total']:.2f}s)",
                flush=True,
            )

    # per-m aggregation
    rows = []
    for m in m_grid:
        sub = [r for r in records if r["m"] == m]
        row = {
            "m": m,
            "auc_roc_mean": summarize(r["auc_roc"] for r in sub)["mean"],
            "auc_roc_std": summarize(r["auc_roc"] for r in sub)["std"],
            "auc_pr_mean": summarize(r["auc_pr"] for r in sub)["mean"],
            "auc_pr_std": summarize(r["auc_pr"] for r in sub)["std"],
            "auc_roc_min": summarize(r["auc_roc"] for r in sub)["min"],
            "auc_roc_max": summarize(r["auc_roc"] for r in sub)["max"],
            "skipped_fraction_mean": float(np.mean([r["skipped_fraction_mean"] for r in sub])),
            "seconds_per_run": float(np.mean([r["partition_seconds_total"] for r in sub])),
        }
        rows.append(row)

    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "per_m_table.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=list(rows[0].keys()))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)

    payload = {
        "dataset": "cardio",
        "provenance": prov,
        "config": {"m_grid": m_grid, "seeds": seeds, "t": t},
        "records": records,
        "per_m": rows,
        "total_seconds": time.perf_counter() - t_start,
    }
    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "raw_cardio.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2)

    best = max(rows, key=lambda r: r["auc_roc_mean"])
    print(f"\nbest m by mean AUC-ROC: {best['m']} "
          f"(auc_roc={best['auc_roc_mean']:.4f} +/- {best['auc_roc_std']:.4f}, "
          f"auc_pr={best['auc_pr_mean']:.4f} +/- {best['auc_pr_std']:.4f})")
    print(f"total {payload['total_seconds']:.1f}s")
    return payload


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--m", type=int, nargs="*", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="*", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--t", type=int, default=T)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="results")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    run(a.m, a.seeds, a.t, a.out)

    expansion (a single BLAS matrix product); the winning squared distance is
    read back with ``min(axis=1)``, which is exactly the entry selected by the
    argmin, so no second distance pass is needed.
    """
    X = np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    A = np.ascontiguousarray(X[anchor_idx], dtype=np.float64)
    n = X.shape[0]
    m = A.shape[0]
    if chunk_rows is None:

    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)

        delta[start:stop] = np.sqrt(np.maximum(d2.min(axis=1), 0.0))

"""Core SVEAD implementation (paper Sections 4.1-4.4, Algorithm 1).

Pipeline per partition k = 1..t
-------------------------------
1. sample m anchors uniformly from the row indices *without replacement*
   (R1, Section 4.1 "Anchor Sampling");
2. assign every point to its nearest anchor by Euclidean distance -- an
   *implicit* Voronoi diagram, no cell boundaries or vertices are built
   (R2 / R11, Section 4.1 "Voronoi Cell Assignment", Eq. (1));
3. for every non-empty cell compute delta_max and delta_mean *before* any
   scoring (R4, Algorithm 1 lines 7-10);
4. score each point as s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean (R3, Eq. (3));
   a cell that contains only its anchor (|C| == 1) is skipped for that
   partition (Section 4.2);
5. average the per-partition scores (R6, Eq. (5)).

The implementation is chunked and O(n*m*d*t) (R12).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from typing import Dict, Tuple

import numpy as np

# Keep the (chunk x m) squared-distance block under ~32 MB of float64.
_MAX_BLOCK_ELEMENTS = 4_000_000


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R1: anchor sampling
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample ``m`` distinct row indices uniformly without replacement."""
    m = int(min(m, n))
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R2 / R11: implicit Voronoi assignment
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _chunk_size(m: int) -> int:
    return max(1, int(_MAX_BLOCK_ELEMENTS // max(1, m)))


def assign_cells(
    X: np.ndarray, anchor_idx: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int | None = None
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Assign every row of ``X`` to its nearest anchor.

    Returns ``(cell_ids, delta)`` where ``cell_ids[i]`` is the index (into
    ``anchor_idx``) of the nearest anchor of row ``i`` and ``delta[i]`` is the
    Euclidean distance to that anchor.  Ties are broken towards the lowest
    anchor index (``np.argmin`` returns the first minimum).

    Squared distances are evaluated with the ``||x-a||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||a||^2
    - 2 x.a`` expansion (one BLAS matrix product); the winning squared
    distance is read back with ``min(axis=1)``, which is exactly the entry
    selected by the argmin, so no second distance pass is needed.
    """
    X = np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    A = np.ascontiguousarray(X[anchor_idx], dtype=np.float64)
    n = X.shape[0]
    m = A.shape[0]
    if chunk_rows is None:
        chunk_rows = _chunk_size(m)

    a_sq = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", A, A)
    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)

    for start in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        stop = min(start + chunk_rows, n)
        block = X[start:stop]
        d2 = (
            np.einsum("ij,ij->i", block, block)[:, None]
            + a_sq[None, :]
            - 2.0 * (block @ A.T)
        )
        j = np.argmin(d2, axis=1)
        cell[start:stop] = j
        # d2.min(axis=1) is exactly d2[row, argmin] -> the winning squared distance
        delta[start:stop] = np.sqrt(np.maximum(d2.min(axis=1), 0.0))
    return cell, delta


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R4: per-cell statistics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def cell_stats(cell: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, m: int) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Per-cell ``delta_max`` / ``delta_mean`` / size, computed before scoring.

    Uses ``bincount`` for the counts and sums and ``maximum.at`` for the
    per-cell maximum, i.e. O(n + m) with no sort.
    """
    cell = np.asarray(cell, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.asarray(delta, dtype=np.float64)
    counts = np.bincount(cell, minlength=m).astype(np.int64)
    sums = np.bincount(cell, weights=delta, minlength=m)

    dmax = np.full(m, -np.inf, dtype=np.float64)
    np.maximum.at(dmax, cell, delta)
    empty = counts == 0

"""Core SVEAD implementation (paper Sections 4.1-4.4, Algorithm 1).

Pipeline per partition k = 1..t
-------------------------------
1. sample m anchors uniformly from the row indices *without replacement*
   (R1, Section 4.1 "Anchor Sampling");
2. assign every point to its nearest anchor by Euclidean distance -- an
   *implicit* Voronoi diagram, no cell boundaries or vertices are built
   (R2 / R11, Section 4.1 "Voronoi Cell Assignment", Eq. (1));
3. for every non-empty cell compute delta_max and delta_mean *before* any
   scoring (R4, Algorithm 1 lines 7-10);
4. score each point as s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean (R3, Eq. (3));
   a cell that contains only its anchor (|C| == 1) is skipped for that
   partition (Section 4.2);
5. average the per-partition scores (R6, Eq. (5)).

The implementation is chunked and O(n*m*d*t) (R12).
"""

import time
from typing import Dict, Tuple

import numpy as np

# Keep the (chunk x m) squared-distance block under ~32 MB of float64.
_MAX_BLOCK_ELEMENTS = 4_000_000


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R1: anchor sampling
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample ``m`` distinct row indices uniformly without replacement."""
    m = int(min(m, n))
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R2 / R11: implicit Voronoi assignment
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

Pipeline per partition k = 1..t
-------------------------------
1. sample m anchors uniformly from the row indices *without replacement*
   (R1, Section 4.1 "Anchor Sampling");
2. assign every point to its nearest anchor by Euclidean distance -- an
   *implicit* Voronoi diagram, no cell boundaries or vertices are built
   (R2 / R11, Section 4.1 "Voronoi Cell Assignment", Eq. (1));
3. for every non-empty cell compute delta_max and delta_mean *before* any
   scoring (R4, Algorithm 1 lines 7-10);
4. score each point as s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean (R3, Eq. (3));

5. average the per-partition scores (R6, Eq. (5)).

``||x-a||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||a||^2 - 2 x.a`` expansion so that the nearest-anchor
search is a single BLAS matrix product per partition; the row-wise minimum of
that block is exactly the squared distance of the winning anchor, so no second
distance pass is required.

    m = int(min(m, n))

def _chunk_size(m: int) -> int:
    return max(1, int(_MAX_BLOCK_ELEMENTS // max(1, m)))

    A column loop is markedly faster than ``min(axis=1)`` for the small ``m``
    values that SVEAD actually uses; the generic reduction wins for large m.

    m = d2.shape[1]

        return out

TOL_C1 = 0.0189

                "mean_mean_cell_size": diag["mean_mean_cell_size"],

target.statement: SVEAD achieves AUC-ROC 0.9339 on the cardio dataset.

tolerance.why: Rule 1: the paper reports AUC-ROC std 0.0063 over 5 runs for cardio (Table 5, row cardio, column VEAD); 3 x 0.0063 = 0.0189, rounded to the 4-decimal precision the paper prints.

audit_summary: The code is a faithful from-paper reimplementation of the SVEAD pipeline in Section 4 / Algorithm 1: uniform without-replacement anchor sampling, implicit nearest-anchor Voronoi assignment, per-cell delta_max/delta_mean computed before scoring, score=(delta/delta_max)*delta_mean with a singleton-cell skip, and an arithmetic mean over t=100 partitions. The target C1 is computed entirely by code (reproduce.py only holds 0.9339 as a comparison constant), and the clean re-run of `python reproduce.py` reproduces 0.9346 +/- 0.0065 over 5 seeds against the paper's 0.9339 (reported std 0.0063) - an absolute gap of 0.0007, far inside the 0.0189 tolerance - with C2 likewise matching (0.5378 vs 0.5356). The dataset is the correct ADBench cardio artifact (validated at 1831x21, 176 anomalies, 9.61%), the metric is AUC-ROC, and the unsupervised full-data protocol matches the stated target, so the experiment identity is correct. The one real fragility is the paper's undisclosed m-selection criterion (A3/A10/A14): the reported value uses m=2, the extreme grid point that maximises mean AUC-ROC on the evaluation labels, and AUC-ROC decays monotonically to 0.6759 at m=256, so agreement depends on that (customary but label-using) criterion - m=4 (0.9218) is also within tolerance, while m>=8 is not. A second ambiguity (Eq. 5 vs Section 4.2 singleton handling, A12/A16) is numerically inert here because the skipped fraction at m=2 is exactly 0, and both aggregation variants are recorded. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k CPU/GPU scalability) are out of scope and correctly marked not reproduced; the C5 probe was measured at 11.5 s for reference versus the paper's <3 s on a Ryzen 9 9950X, a device-specific claim that cannot be adjudicated on this machine. No hard-coded/echoed result numbers, no wrong split, no proxy metric and no substitute method were found; the full m-grid x 5 seeds at t=100 was run, so nothing was scaled down for the match target.

requirement_check.evidence: svead/svead_core.py sample_anchors() uses rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False); experiments/checks.py asserts 20 random (m,seed) pairs all yield m distinct indices.
assign_cells() computes nearest anchor by the exact squared-Euclidean expansion ||x||^2+||a||^2-2x.a and takes row-wise argmin (ties -> lowest index, A5); no cell geometry is built.
score_partition() implements s = (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean per Eq. (3); delta is the point-to-anchor distance and delta_max/delta_mean are per-cell statistics.
cell_stats() computes delta_max, delta_mean and counts (bincount / maximum.at) for every cell before any scoring; checks.py asserts delta_mean>0 for all non-singleton cells.

svead_score() accumulates per-partition scores and returns total/max(count,1); at the selected m=2 the skipped fraction is exactly 0.0 for all 5 runs, so this is bit-identical to the literal /t mean, and metrics.json also records the literal sum_over_t variant (auc_roc_sum_over_t) for every run.

Full m grid {2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256} = {2^1..2^8} is run with t fixed at 100 in reproduce.py (M_GRID, T=100); the selection criterion is not stated by the paper and is assumed to be argmax mean AUC-ROC (A3/A10/A14, disclosed in metrics.json).
Seeds 1..5 give 5 repeats per m; C1 reports the mean 0.934576 +/- 0.00647 (std, ddof=1) with per-run values [0.9365,0.9427,0.9377,0.9284,0.9276].
svead/metrics.py computes AUC-ROC (roc_auc_score) and AUC-PR (average_precision_score, ADBench/PyOD convention) plus a trapezoidal PR variant; both primary metrics are reported.

The scoring path (svead_core, data loader) never receives y; metrics.evaluate(scores, y) consumes labels strictly after scores exist. Caveat: the reported C1 uses the m that maximises mean AUC-ROC over the grid on the same evaluation labels, a disclosed label-using grid-search step (A3/A10/A14) that is customary in ADBench benchmarking but does make the chosen configuration metric-selected.
Only nearest-anchor queries are used; no Voronoi vertices/edges or cell-boundary construction appears anywhere in svead_core.py.

Per partition work is O(n*m*d) (one BLAS matmul plus O(n+m) cell stats) and the ensemble loops t times => O(n*m*d*t); the scaling probe is approximately linear in n (0.87 s @50k, 1.98 s @100k, 4.05 s @200k, 11.54 s @500k, d=10, m=2, t=100).
